title: Python project setup: venv and requirements
when: A Python project needs setup instructions or a requirements file, or the user asks how to run the code on a fresh machine.
prompt:
Goal: A README setup section and project files that let anyone create an isolated environment and run the project in a few commands.
Steps:
1. State the minimum Python version and how to check it (python3 --version).
2. Show creation and activation: python3 -m venv .venv, then source .venv/bin/activate on POSIX shells or .venv\Scripts\activate on other systems.
3. requirements.txt: a single comment line when only the standard library is used, otherwise exact pins with ==.
4. Give run and test commands exactly as typed (python -m app, python -m unittest).
5. Add .venv/, __pycache__/ and *.pyc to .gitignore.
6. Troubleshooting list: command not found, wrong interpreter, activation blocked by script policy.
Quality bar:
- Every command is in a fenced block and pastes as is.
- Works on a machine with only Python installed.
- Nothing is installed globally.
Pitfalls:
- pip install with sudo.
- Committing the .venv folder.
- Listing packages the code never imports.
Verify:
- [ ] README has a Setup section with fenced commands.
- [ ] requirements.txt exists.
- [ ] .gitignore lists .venv.
- [ ] Run and test commands match real entry points.
Output: README.md with Setup and Run sections, requirements.txt and .gitignore.

examples.input: como alguém roda meu projeto python do zero?
examples.output: README Setup: python3 -m venv .venv, activate per shell, requirements.txt stdlib note, run and test commands
